messages:
alex: Heads-up — I prototyped a header-based canary switch for the API gateway: X-Canary: <id|percent>. Idea is to let us target specific calls without touching route paths. Thoughts on semantics and safety?

maria: I like header toggles for dev testing, but we need clear rules: does X-Canary with a percent mean 'attempt to route with sampling', or is it an absolute override?

alex: Prototype uses two modes: if value is 'id:ABC' we route deterministically by hashing request id+key; if value is 'pct:20' it's sampling-based. Default mode (no header) uses weighted routing by config.

ken: Deterministic by id is handy for repros. But be careful with caching/KV caches — routing the same session to different variants will poison caches. We should document "sticky by client_id" option.

linda: Also need quota implications. If we route one customer to canary and they hit quota, do we count against canary capacity or main? We need per-route and per-model quota accounting in telemetry.

alex: Good call — I wired telemetry tags: route.variant, canary.id, effective_weight. That way billing and SLO dashboards can filter. Example policy JSON I was thinking of: ```json
{"match": {"path": "/v1/generate"}, "split": [{"variant":"v1","weight":80}, {"variant":"v2-canary","weight":20}], "overrides": {"header":"X-Canary","modes": ["id","pct"], "sticky_by": ["client_id","api_key"]}}
```

maria: UX question: how does this show up in Console? We shouldn't expose raw headers to product owners. Suggest Console show 'Target: all / A/B by % / Targeted IDs' with a small advanced toggle that maps to header values for debugging.

ken: Agreed on console. Also rounding: 20% on low QPS routes might select zero requests during short windows. We need a hybrid: sampling + minimum token bucket to guarantee a few test requests per minute when weight>0.

linda: For telemetry: add counters for "canary_hits", "canary_errors", and latency histograms per variant. Also track quota usage per variant and emit events when variant exceeds X% of total quota consumption.

alex: Implementation note: at gateway level we'll evaluate header override before policy lookup, but we must validate header sources (only internal services + console can set it). We'll reject header-based routing from public clients. Plan: require X-Canary-Auth token for header overrides, and gateway will strip header before forwarding to backend.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: gateway/canary-header-checks v0.1 -> staging at 1715008000 :rocket:

maria: Tests needed: 1) deterministic routing reproducibility; 2) sticky_by respects chosen key; 3) telemetry tags are present; 4) header injection blocked for external requests. I'll add e2e matrix.

ken: One more gotcha — function/tool-calls in chat flows might include embedded URLs and user-supplied ids; hashing on those can be unstable. Recommend hashing stable client_id + request_id if available.

alex: Thanks — I'll update the prototype to use client_id fallback and add the Console UX mock. Opening a PR with the gateway changes and a spec doc for ops + billing teams.
